payload.summary: All three amendments are well-founded and I concur with the planner positions. The redundant registry recomputation is a real hot-path inefficiency with an inconsistent mix of registry sources. The denitrification comment is mechanistically backwards. The ROL change conflated two opposing effects by removing root O₂ demand from the baseline.

votes.rationale: Verified: `root_oxygenation_active_biomass_g()` at line 140 calls `compute_habitat_registry(state)` to rebuild the full registry, while other functions in the same file (lines 708, 719, 831) read from `state.habitat_registry` directly. This creates both a performance issue (redundant O(n) recomputation on every tick via `substrate_oxygenation_breakdown` → `root_oxygenation_active_biomass_g`) and an inconsistency where different parts of the same breakdown calculation may see different registry snapshots. Threading a single registry snapshot through the hot path, while keeping the recomputation as a fallback for the standalone `root_oxygenation_bonus_cm()` public accessor, is the right approach.

The comment at lines 131-132 states 'deeper oxic zone → larger suboxic zone pushed deeper → more capacity', implying planted substrates should show MORE denitrification. This is mechanistically incorrect: a deeper oxic zone displaces suboxic volume, leaving LESS room for denitrification. The test at line 168 (`root_oxygenation_reduces_hourly_denitrification_when_it_shrinks_suboxic_volume`) directly demonstrates this — it asserts that planted suboxic pore volume is smaller (line 177) and that planted denitrification export is lower (line 183). The test's assertion (divergence > 0.001) happens to pass regardless of direction, so the code is functionally fine, but the misleading comment could cause a future developer to 'fix' the test in the wrong direction.

Confirmed by reading `estimate_substrate_o2_demand_rate()` (lines 212-238): the function only accounts for decomposer biomass BOD and microfauna respiration. Lines 208-209 explicitly state 'rooted biomass does not also alter the base diffusive penetration term.' This means with `rol_rate_cm_per_g = 0`, a planted bed produces identical O₂ penetration depth as an unplanted bed — the rooted biomass contributes zero additional O₂ demand AND zero O₂ supply. The prior model presumably included root respiration in the demand side, so removing it while adding the ROL supply bonus conflates two opposing biological mechanisms into one parameter. The base model should retain the root-respiration O₂ demand so that `rol_rate_cm_per_g` solely controls the supply-side ROL effect.
